headline: Extra race and MotoGP lift revenue, but diluted EPS dips
summary_short: Liberty Formula One's Q1 2026 revenue rose 59.1% y/y to $711M on one additional Grand Prix and MotoGP's first Q1 in the consolidated base, while diluted EPS fell to $0.03 from $0.05 even as basic net income rose to $57M from $22M.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $711M ($617M Formula 1 + $94M MotoGP) on an extra Grand Prix (3 vs 2 run in Q1), fee escalators, and season-based revenue-recognition timing (3/22nds vs 2/24nds). Operating income swung to $64M from a $67M loss, helped by the absence of 2025's one-time $50M Concorde incentive payment to F1 teams. Basic EPS rose to $0.23, but diluted EPS fell to $0.03: a $48M adjustment reversing the unrealized fair-value gain on the dilutive convertible notes cut diluted earnings to $9M. Cash fell 57.7% y/y to $1,332M and long-term debt rose to $5,021M on the $3,659M MotoGP acquisition closed July 2025. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: One additional F1 Event (3 vs 2) plus contractual fee escalators and calendar-driven revenue-recognition timing (3/22nds vs 2/24nds) lifted F1 revenue $177M; MotoGP added $94M, its first Q1 in Liberty's results since the July 2025 acquisition.
Tracks the revenue drivers above: cost of motorsport revenue rose $118M (F1) against a much larger consolidated revenue increase, per the segment note tables.

2025's quarter carried a one-time $50M Concorde incentive payment to F1 teams (signing bonus for the new Concorde Agreement) that did not recur in 2026, on top of the added-race and fee-escalator revenue growth.
Same underlying causes as EBIT and operating income: added race, fee escalators, and no repeat of 2025's one-time $50M Concorde incentive charge, before the D&A add-back.
Swung from a $67M loss to $64M income, driven by the absence of 2025's one-time $50M Concorde incentive payment plus the added-race and fee-escalator revenue growth described above.
Moves with operating income (added race, fee escalators, no repeat Concorde charge); the release does not separately explain items between operating and pretax income.
Net earnings attributable to Liberty Formula One stockholders rose to $57M from $22M on the same segment growth and absent one-time Concorde charge described above.
Directly follows the $57M (vs $22M) basic earnings attributable to Liberty Formula One stockholders divided by a 251M (vs 249M) weighted average share count.
A $48M adjustment reversing the unrealized fair-value gain on the dilutive 2.25% convertible notes cut diluted earnings to $9M (from $57M basic) on a 261M diluted share count, per the EPS note.
F1's own liquidity discussion cites $19M of capital expenditures at the segment level this quarter; the release does not explain the y/y decline in the $20M consolidated total.
Reflects the $3,659M MotoGP acquisition closed July 2025, funded with cash on hand plus $1.0 billion of new Incremental Term Loan borrowings.
Reflects the $1.0 billion of Incremental Term Loan A/B borrowings drawn to help fund the July 2025 MotoGP acquisition.

An extra Grand Prix, fee escalators, and MotoGP's first full Q1 drove revenue and operating income higher, aided by the absent 2025 one-time $50M Concorde charge; cash fell and debt rose from July 2025's $3.66B MotoGP acquisition, and a note fair-value adjustment cut diluted EPS despite higher basic EPS.
